Story description: Next.js 16 introduces `updateTag()` (read-your-writes: surfaces a user's own change immediately from cache) and `refresh()` (fetches fresh uncached dynamic data without touching the cache). Without these, booking confirmation pages and enquiry acknowledgements show stale data, eroding guest trust. The existing `revalidateTag()` single-argument call is also deprecated in Next.js 16 and must be updated.
acceptanceCriteria: E2E test covers the user flow introduced by US-229
Test navigates to relevant page(s) and asserts on visible state
Test passes in headless browser (Playwright/Cypress/similar)

stories.title: [Security Test] Audit and fix WCAG 2.1 SC 4.1.2 Name, Role, Value for all interactive elements
stories.description: Write security tests for auth/permission logic in US-230. Story description: SC 4.1.2 (Level A) requires every interactive element to have a programmatically determinable name, role, and state. Custom buttons, icon-only controls, gallery navigation arrows, and booking CTAs are common failure points. This is the single most frequently violated WCAG criterion globally and a Level A requirement — non-compliance constitutes a complete accessibility failure at WCAG 2.1 AA level.
acceptanceCriteria: Security test covers access control introduced by US-230
Test verifies unauthorized access is blocked (401/403 responses)
No sensitive data (tokens, passwords) leaked in error responses

stories.title: [E2E Test] Implement WCAG 2.1 SC 2.2.2 Pause/Stop/Hide for auto-advancing animated content
stories.description: Write end-to-end user flow test for the feature in US-234. Story description: SC 2.2.2 (Level A) requires that any content that moves, blinks, or auto-updates for more than 5 seconds must provide a mechanism to pause, stop, or hide it. This is separate from respecting `prefers-reduced-motion` — it requires a visible UI control users can activate regardless of OS settings. Hero carousels, scrolling announcements, and animated social proof counters are common failure points.
